findings.title: Falsehood without renewal
findings.claim: Through the focus's repeated الْبَٰطِلُ, the wider arrival formula in 34:49 gives the ever-perishing statement a non-renewal edge: falsehood neither begins anew nor returns.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries al-bāṭil as the subject that vanishes and then predicates zahūqan of it. In 34:49 the arrival frame is followed by a separate clause denying al-bāṭil initiation and return. That clause contacts the focus's repeated al-bāṭil and makes its perishing legible as inability to reconstitute.
findings.reader_payoff: The final predicate can be heard as a claim about falsehood's inability to renew itself, as well as its passing after truth arrives.
findings.containment: This is a wider surface-level resonance that adds to the focus's direct declaration. It does not claim that 34:49 causes the focus event, that every historical falsehood has already ceased, or that the target's unsupplied morphology is known.

epistemic.reason: The candidate source is legacy_unbound; 34:49 supplies exact Arabic for the parallel, but its target morphology and lexical analysis are not included. The focus carriers and branch facets are supplied directly.

branch_activations.activation: The added non-renewal clause, rather than the repeated arrival wording, contacts the focus's arrival event and makes it a threshold after which falsehood has no new beginning or return.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Truth's arrival is read in the wider echo as exposing falsehood's inability to restart.

findings.title: Contact and selective persistence
findings.claim: Wider echoes make the focus's truth-arrival and falsehood-passing a dynamic encounter with unequal persistence: 21:18 places truth upon falsehood before its vanishing, while 13:17 gives the contrast an image in which foam goes away and what benefits remains.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries الْحَقُّ, الْبَٰطِلُ, and زَهَقَ / زَهُوقًا in one declaration. The supplied 21:18 surface puts truth onto falsehood and describes its destruction and vanishing; 13:17 names truth and falsehood in a parable whose foam departs while beneficial matter remains. These triggers return through the focus pair and its passing predicate, changing the sequence into contact followed by selective persistence.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the declaration as more than a winner and a loser: the wider images make visible how what lacks a ground passes while what benefits can remain.
findings.containment: The water-and-foam image is analogical and does not identify every instance of falsehood with foam or claim that 13:17 causes the focus event. The target surfaces are supplied, but their morphology and lexical analysis are not.

epistemic.reason: The narrowed candidate source is legacy_unbound. The contextual surfaces at 21:18 and 13:17 are supplied and independently show the stated contact and persistence contrast, while target morphology remains unavailable.

findings.title: Arrival amid resistance
findings.claim: The wider record separates truth's arrival from shared acceptance: 43:78 says most of its hearers dislike the truth brought to them, while 10:108 leaves guidance and misguidance with each recipient. This makes the focus's declaration compatible with continuing resistance without weakening its statement about falsehood's passing.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries جَآءَ ٱلْحَقُّ as a truth-arrival relation. The supplied surfaces at 43:78 and 10:108 repeat the arrival of truth but attach resistance or recipient-level response; their contact changes the global reading from an assumed common reception to a decisive arrival amid continued disagreement and choice.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the focus's verdict and the fact of resistance together, without taking falsehood's passing to mean that every hearer recognizes or accepts the truth at once.
findings.containment: This concerns reception, not a denial of the focus's declarative force or a claim about every hearer. The contextual parallels are grounded in supplied Arabic surfaces; their target morphology is not supplied.
